bootstrap.why: The planning document lists it as a core command with no body (15.1) and makes it the precondition for Protected machine mode (8.1: an elevated broker must not trust user-writable Skill code). A real bootstrap creates the root marker and the ACL layout, and that is protected state. The other half of what the name carries -- the 9.8 re-entry sweep (read marker and generation, scan AIROOT's own directories, collect external candidates, report classifications, plan only what the user picked) -- is today's doctor + discover + plan, so no part of it survives as a plain file write either.

reconcile.why: Draft 60 first filed this as 'covered-elsewhere' on the reading that its content is already doctor (re-observation drift) + desired evaluation + plan, and the audit found that reading wrong. 15.1 defines it as 'reconcile <manifest>', the roadmap puts it in P6 directly after project manifest and project binding (19), and the shipped CLI already says as much: forget reports project_manifest_check='not_implemented_before_p6' (the same rule 15.5 states for unadopt: a reference still used by a project manifest must not be released). Nothing in P1 produces or reads a project manifest, so the verb has no input it could honestly consume. The overlap with doctor/desired/plan is real, but it is the smaller half of the command -- recorded here instead of being used as the category.

path backup.why: The planning document lists it in P2's deliverables next to the ACL baseline, the single machine PATH entry and the elevated broker (19), and it exists to precede a machine PATH change. Recording the current PATH read-only is not the semantics the command is defined by; shipping a read-only verb under this name would make the real one look done.

path restore.why: Restoring PATH is a machine PATH write, which needs the broker. The loose-first direction (ADR-0021) does not reach this one: a restore is not a read, so there is no weaker form of it to ship.

root adopt.why: The rules are no longer missing: ADR-0025 decided them (source untouched, verify before switch, one atomic switch point, and adopt itself writes no machine PATH). What is left is the switch, and that is protected state -- it moves the active-root pointer and, for the relocate spelling, the single allowed machine PATH entry, which is why 8.1.1 pairs adopt with restore-from-backup as two answers to an identity mismatch. 8.1.1 and 15.5 already name the checks (root marker, volume identity, protocol/schema, registry integrity); ADR-0025 decides the copy/verify/switch half and files the remaining blocker here.

root relocate.why: 15.5 defines it as migrating the whole AIROOT\cli data root: establish the new root marker, copy and verify the persistent data, then switch the active root. The switch moves the machine PATH entry, and the frozen contract allows exactly one AIROOT entry there (AGENTS.md, section 5, item 8). A directory copy cannot do that, so it is a protected commit.

approve.why_no_lane: A lane is a question an agent can act on. ADR-0025's D1 left the protected broker to P2, and since ADR-0046 this machine *can* sign a token -- but only as an explicit local step (`airoot.tx.issuer` provisions the key, then issues), because no CLI verb mints one. A lane ending at `approve` would still point at a step the CLI cannot take for the agent, so the honesty block says this in prose instead.

install.why_no_lane: Same reason as `approve`: it needs a token, and no CLI verb mints one -- signing is a deliberate local step (ADR-0046), while ADR-0025's D1 is what keeps the broker half waiting for P2. The plan-shaped part of the question does have lanes (`plan`, `scope decide`), which is what an agent can actually complete today.

extension.why_no_lane: Extension diagnostics (`extension list`, `extension status <id> --operation <status|probe|invoke>`). It is not on an agent's question surface: SKILL.md's command map does not carry it, and an agent that meets an extension meets it through `search implementations`, which has a lane.

unadopt.why_no_lane: It is the frozen name from the planning document for what is clearer as `forget`; the CLI registers it as a compatibility alias, so it has no question of its own and `forget` carries the lane.

scope.why_not_mapped: `scope decide` is the routing decision surfaced on its own; the command map's `plan` row already routes *and* plans (`--scope`/`--target`/`--dry-run`), so teaching both would present one decision twice. Its lane stays because it answers without producing a plan.

uninstall.why_not_mapped: It is `tool retire` + `tool gc` in one verb (`retire then collect an owned payload, needs approval`). The map teaches those two graded steps on purpose: retiring clears the binding, collecting is what deletes, and the gate sits at `tool gc --apply` -- one verb would hide the grading. The composed path also needs a token that no CLI verb mints (ADR-0046: signing is an explicit local step).

honesty.security_mode_note: P1 is policy_only: enforcement is convention and audit, not ACL. A same-user process can bypass it.
honesty.degradation_note: CURRENT_SOURCE_DEGRADED (exit 2) is a normal fallback to a healthy reference, not a failure.
honesty.signature_note: v1 verifies published digests only. A digest is not a signature; never imply the artifact was signed.
honesty.document_schema_note: `document_schema` names the published schema that describes the document a lane's `read` paths live in, or null when no schema describes it. A null is **measured**, not assumed: the CLI is run, and every published document schema is tried against what it printed (cli/tests/test_l1_agent_read_fields.py). 5 of 34 lanes are pinned (doctor, where x2, inventory, search); the other 29 read a report whose shape only the field-existence check holds. Two of the 29 print a self-validated plan **plus** `plan_file` / `required_action` / `reason_code`, which are deliberately not part of the plan contract. **Why no report schema pins the rest** (measured, draft §100): the 29 reports have 29 distinct top-level shapes, so one schema either fails them all or would need `additionalProperties: true` — a published contract that accepts any extra key, which the doctrine refuses as a capability that only looks safe. What they do share is exactly `schema_version` and `reason_code`, and that much is guarded. Treat a null lane's fields as informational and never quote them as contract.
honesty.allowed_claims: See AGENTS.md §8. Never claim AIROOT is implemented, available, or Everything-class.
